Kill switch: a key that names its server without addresses connects while the block holds on Linux too. The service's own lookup asked only 127.0.0.53, as .NET reads /etc/resolv.conf, which names systemd-resolved's stub alone, and the block stops the stub's own lookups. A resolver on the machine itself is now skipped, and on Linux, where none is left, systemd-resolved's upstream list (/run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf) stands in Tested: on the Ubuntu 26.04 and Windows Server 2025 Desktop VMs against the server VM, a key rewritten to 192-168-250-30.sslip.io with no addresses - under lockdown, after a person's disconnect, the person's own lookup fails and the service looks the name up itself and connects; Ubuntu failed before the fix ("Could not resolve any host endpoint"), Windows passed as it was.
